bar: Company guide: Q3 call (2026-06-25) guided Q4 consolidated core EBITDA up roughly $40-50m sequentially from $353.6m (NA Steel +~$40m from the absence of a $20m outage headwind plus volume/margin, Construction Solutions mid-teens adjusted-EBITDA growth, Europe ex-CO2 +$3-5m but reported Europe down because the $20.4m CO2 credit does not recur) — https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026 and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm. Consensus adjusted EPS: Benzinga $2.00 / $2.54bn revenue (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CMC/earnings-forecasts), Stocktwits $1.98 / $2.57bn (https://stocktwits.com/symbol/CMC/earnings), MarketBeat $1.93 on 1 estimate (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CMC/earnings/), Zacks $1.91. Sized against $1.93-2.00 adjusted EPS and the company's own EBITDA guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.3M shares, 5.7% of shares outstanding, 5.2 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, up marginally from 6.1M (08-31) and 6.2M (09-15) — https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/ (fetched 2026-10-14). Not crowded; a July reading was 4.7M / 3.6 DTC. Skew: +26.81 vol points (25d put over call), 'downside paid', but total open interest is 495 contracts and the ATM spread is 62% of mid, so the skew is a thin-chain artefact as much as a statement; put/call OI 0.39. Stock -21.7% from its 52-week high, 20d run-up -1.0%, 5d +3.0%; it fell 3.87% on 3.4x volume on 2026-09-18 in sympathy with Nucor's below-consensus Q3 guide (https://ts2.tech/en/nucor-stock-falls-6-3-after-5-60-profit-midpoint-misses-estimates/); JPMorgan cut its PT to $83 from $86 on 2026-09-09, Overweight kept (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CMC/price-targets).

findings.finding: The Jun-Aug quarter CMC reports tomorrow overlaps the quarter both EAF peers pre-guided on 2026-09-17: Steel Dynamics said steel profitability would be 'significantly higher' on metal-margin expansion, record shipments, higher realised selling values and LOWER scrap costs with backlog ~50% above a year ago and non-residential construction leading demand; Nucor guided steel mills up on higher ASPs and stable volumes and its rebar-fabrication-heavy steel products segment up on higher volumes and pricing. Scrap settlements over CMC's quarter were flat to down (SMU: July soft-sideways, August busheling -$5/gt and shredded -$5/gt to $457.50/$417.50) while US long-product prices held flat-to-up on tight rebar supply and data-center demand, so the $40-50m sequential core-EBITDA guide (to ~$395-405m) and the $1.93-2.00 EPS consensus look reachable or beatable; CMC's Q3 metal margin was $610/t on a $989/t ASP against $379/t scrap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name does not pay for the quarter: the 2025-10-16 annual print beat ($1.37 vs $1.34) and fell 7.26% on the outlook; 2026-03-26 missed ($1.16 vs $1.28) and fell 4.69%; 2026-06-25 beat modestly ($1.73 vs $1.70) and rose 3.94% on an improved Q4 EBITDA outlook (https://www.rttnews.com/story.aspx?Id=3634292). Baseline 4 up / 3 down, median |move| 3.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: both peer guides are a month old and CMC's consensus already sits near the guide. What is not in the price is the content of those guides as opposed to their headline: both peers guided BELOW consensus and CMC fell 3.87% on 3.4x volume the same day (https://ts2.tech/en/nucor-stock-falls-6-3-after-5-60-profit-midpoint-misses-estimates/) although both said long-product margins widened and scrap fell, which is the half of their statement that applies to a rebar producer. If the market had priced the content rather than the headline, CMC would not sit 21.7% below its 52-week high with the 20-day run-up at -1.0%.
findings.independence: Nucor 2026-09-17 guidance (steel mills up on ASPs, steel products up on volume and price): https://s202.q4cdn.com/531038915/files/doc_news/Nucor-Announces-Guidance-for-the-Third-Quarter-of-2026-Earnings-2026.pdf. SMU August scrap settlement: https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/08/11/smu-scrap-prices-stagnant-in-august/. SMU July: https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/07/14/smus-scrap-tags-settle-soft-sideways-in-july/. SteelOrbis US long-steel headlines 2026-08-26 ('flat amid support from data centers, tight supplies') and 2026-09-03 ('stable to up on tight rebar supply and steady demand'): https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-prices/steel-prices-market-analyses/longs-and-billet/rebar?page=3. All are proxies; CMC's own Q4 numbers are not public.

findings.finding: The line this stock trades on is the forward outlook, and the series that bear on the FY27 Q1 (Sep-Nov) guide lean soft: SteelOrbis 2026-10-08 reports US long-steel prices 'mostly flat as markets evaluate higher October scrap trade' (October scrap trading higher against flat rebar, a metal-margin squeeze at the start of the new quarter); SteelOrbis 2026-09-24 reports US long-steel prices stabilising 'amid reduced construction-related activity' citing a 2026-09-21 Dodge Construction Network report; the Q3 call already flagged West Virginia carrying costs doubling to ~$8-10m a quarter before saleable product, the mill's hot commissioning slipping from June to 'later in the summer' on ~100 days of weather delay, and a $60-65m per quarter gap between core EBITDA and pre-tax earnings from precast purchase accounting and interest for the next two quarters. Against that, the next semiannual Polish CO2 credit (~$20m) lands in Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what has moved this stock: -7.26% on 2025-10-16 (same annual print, Q1 outlook), -4.69% on 2026-03-26, +3.94% on 2026-06-25 when the Q4 EBITDA outlook improved (https://www.rttnews.com/story.aspx?Id=3634292).
findings.why_not_priced: The put skew (+26.8 vol points) says the market is paying for exactly this, so the direction is partly priced; what is not priced is the magnitude the company will put on it. If the market had priced a soft Q1 guide the consensus FY27 estimates would have been cut after 2026-09-17 and they were not (JPMorgan trimmed its PT $86 to $83 on 09-09 and kept Overweight; no September/October rating changes found).
findings.independence: Proxies, not company numbers: SteelOrbis 2026-09-24 (Dodge-cited reduced construction activity): https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-prices/steel-prices-market-analyses/longs-and-billet/us-long-steel-prices-stabilize-as-q4-nears-amid-reduced-construction-related-activity-1479698.htm; SMU September scrap (busheling +$10/gt, shredded and HMS flat): https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/09/08/smu-scrap-tags-for-shredded-hms-flat-while-busheling-ticks-up/; Fastmarkets notes the October Chicago busheling settlement was delayed past 10-09 with markets not yet settled: https://www.fastmarkets.com/insights/delayed-publication-of-fastmarkets-north-american-ferrous-scrap-prices-for-october/. WV costs and purchase-accounting gap are the company's own words on the Q3 call: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026 (shares that document with the bar). The offset (STLD's backlog through Q1 2027 and 'persistently low customer inventories', 2026-09-17) is in the first finding's source.

findings.finding: The bar was reset lower before the print by someone else's miss: CMC closed $64.50 on 2026-09-18, down 3.87% on 3.43x its 10-session average volume, in sympathy with Nucor (-6.32%) and Steel Dynamics guiding below consensus, and it sits 21.7% below its 52-week high with a 20-day run-up of -1.0% into an annual print; short interest at 5.7% / 5.2 days to cover is not crowded, and the 495-contract option chain quoting a 62% ATM spread is too thin for its 26.8-point put skew to be a reliable positioning statement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior instance in the baseline; the Oct 2025 annual print fell 7.26% from a higher starting point.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, filed because the sympathy move was on a peer's headline rather than on any CMC number; if the market had re-priced CMC on its own guide the September drop would have come with estimate cuts, and the Q4 consensus has held at $1.93-2.00 since August.
findings.independence: Short interest: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest/ (settlement 2026-09-30). Analyst actions: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CMC/price-targets (JPM 2026-09-09). Baseline tape and option fields in the sealed file.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-05 the board added $600m to the buyback (total capacity ~$717m) and on the Q3 call management said repurchases return 'to a more elevated level' once net leverage reaches 2x, which it was at 2.1x with a target of below 2x by mid-2027 'or sooner'; tomorrow's release is the first with a full quarter of the lower-capex run-rate (FY27 capex ~$350m vs ~$550m in FY26) and a seasonally strong cash quarter, so the print can show leverage at or under 2x and a resumed repurchase cadence.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback-driven reaction in the seven-print baseline; the 2026-08-05 authorisation itself produced no large move (stock traded ~$67-72 in August per the analyst snapshots).
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is priced (two months old); the timing of its use is not — the company tied it to a leverage level that the Q4 cash flow can cross. If the market expected an immediate resumption, the stock would not have given back the Investor Day move and more.
findings.independence: Leverage and buyback conditionality from the Q3 call: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026 (shares that document with finding 2 and the bar). Investor Day targets release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/22444/000119312526333797/d95091dex991.htm.

findings.finding: Polish long-steel demand was 'still weak' in mid-August with rebar assessed flat at 2,650-2,680 zloty/t and no transactions heard (Fastmarkets via Eurometal, week to 2026-08-14), against management's June description of Polish demand as 'really good' and a guide for Europe Steel Group operational EBITDA (ex-CO2) up $3-5m sequentially; Europe was ~10% of Q3 core EBITDA ($34.7m incl. the $20.4m CO2 credit), so a miss on the ex-CO2 guide is small net of the rest of the company.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe has not been the line this stock moved on in the baseline; the segment was near break-even a year ago ($3.6m).
findings.why_not_priced: Niche series (Polish zloty assessments) that no US preview carries; the reported Europe number will be down anyway on the CO2 non-recurrence, which the company guided, so the market is told to expect a decline and may not distinguish the operational miss within it.
findings.independence: The guide it is measured against is the Q3 call: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026. Nothing else independent found; Polish construction output for August/September was not located.

baseline_tension: The skew (+26.8 vol points, downside paid) agrees with the soft-outlook finding and cuts against the quarter and positioning findings; the near-flat 20-day run-up and the September sympathy drop say the bar was lowered by a peer's headline, not by CMC's own numbers, so the net is a slight negative lean rather than agreement with the skew.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guided range) and rule 1 (this name sells the quarter and trades the outlook; the same annual print fell 7.3% on a beat last October): Q4 quarter finding shrunk +1.5 → +0.8

Rule 5 (proxies the company has not confirmed — SteelOrbis headlines, a Dodge report cited second-hand, Eurometal): FY27 Q1 outlook finding shrunk −2.0 → −1.5 and filed as a proxy rather than left out
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): Poland finding shrunk −0.3 → −0.2 against a ~10%-of-EBITDA segment whose reported decline is already guided

Rule 7 (positioning): skew +26.8 agrees with the negative and the chain is 495 contracts at a 62% spread, short interest 5.7% / 5.2 DTC not crowded — no further change to signs; buyback finding trimmed +0.5 → +0.4 as partly priced since 2026-08-05
